title: Food, and verbs that change their vowel (Essen)
summary: Name everyday food and say what you eat. Some verbs change their vowel with du and er/sie/es: essen, du isst; nehmen, du nimmst.
goals: Say what you eat for breakfast
Use essen, nehmen, lesen, sehen and fahren with du and er/sie/es

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 11: Eating and leisure (Lebensmittel)
Nicos Weg A1, chapter 3: In company (Eine Pizza bitte!)

points: Irregular (strong) verbs change the vowel of their stem in the present, but only with [[du]] and [[er]]/[[sie]]/[[es]]. The endings are the regular ones.
e becomes i: [[sprechen]], [[du sprichst]]; [[treffen]], [[du triffst]]; [[essen]], [[du isst]]. [[nehmen]] changes more: [[du nimmst]], [[er nimmt]].
e becomes ie: [[lesen]], [[du liest]]; [[sehen]], [[du siehst]].
a becomes ä, and au becomes äu: [[fahren]], [[du fährst]]; [[waschen]], [[du wäschst]]; [[laufen]], [[du läufst]].
[[wissen]] is special: it changes with [[ich]] too: [[ich weiß]], [[du weißt]], [[er weiß]].
Not every verb with these vowels is irregular: [[lernen]] stays [[du lernst]]. Learn the irregular ones one by one.
notes.extra: [[laufen]], [[waschen]], [[treffen]], [[sehen]] and [[wissen]], beyond the lesson's four verbs.

points: [[die Lebensmittel]] (food, groceries) is plural.
Some foods have no plural: [[das Wasser]], [[die Milch]], [[die Butter]], [[das Eis]] (ice cream), [[der Reis]], [[der Zucker]]. [[die Pommes]] (chips) has no singular.
Some have two articles: [[das Sandwich]] or [[der Sandwich]], [[die Cola]] or [[das Cola]] (the south says das), [[der Joghurt]] or [[das Joghurt]].
[[die Pizza]] has two plurals: [[die Pizzas]] or [[die Pizzen]].

The rest: [[der Kuchen]], [[das Brot]], [[der Apfel]], [[die Banane]], [[der Käse]], [[die Karotte]], [[der Salat]], [[die Wurst]], [[der Kaffee]], [[der Tee]], [[die Kartoffel]], [[das Ei]], [[die Tomate]].
[[das Frühstück]] is breakfast, and [[frühstücken]] the verb.
Drinks: [[der Kaffee]], [[der Tee]], [[die Milch]], [[der Saft]] ([[der Apfelsaft]], [[der Orangensaft]]), [[der Smoothie]].
Rolls depend on the region: [[das Brötchen]] in most of Germany, [[die Semmel]] in Bavaria and Austria, [[die Schrippe]] in Berlin. A pretzel is [[die Brezel]], in Bavaria [[die Breze]].

On the table: [[das Brot]], [[der Toast]], [[das Croissant]], [[das Müsli]], [[der Joghurt]], [[die Butter]], [[die Marmelade]] (jam), [[der Honig]], [[der Käse]], [[die Wurst]], [[der Schinken]] (ham), [[der Speck]] (bacon), [[das Obst]].
Eggs: [[das Spiegelei]] (fried), [[das Rührei]] (scrambled), [[das gekochte Ei]] (boiled).
Talking about it: [[Zum Frühstück esse ich eine Banane und trinke einen Kaffee.]]

phrases.de: Zum Frühstück esse ich eine Banane und trinke einen Kaffee.
phrases.en: For breakfast I eat a banana and drink a coffee.

phrases.de: Zum Frühstück esse ich eine Scheibe Brot mit Käse.
phrases.en: For breakfast I eat a slice of bread with cheese.

notes.extra: Regional words for rolls ([[Semmel]], [[Schrippe]]), the three kinds of egg, and [[Zum Frühstück ...]].

points: [[das Obst]] (fruit) is a collective noun: singular, with das.

Common fruit: [[der Apfel]], [[die Banane]], [[die Birne]] (pear), [[die Orange]], [[die Kirsche]] (cherry), [[die Traube]] (grape), [[die Pflaume]] (plum), [[der Pfirsich]] (peach), [[die Aprikose]] (apricot).
Berries: [[die Erdbeere]] (strawberry), [[die Himbeere]] (raspberry), [[die Brombeere]] (blackberry), [[die Heidelbeere]] or [[die Blaubeere]] (blueberry).
More: [[die Melone]], [[die Wassermelone]], [[die Ananas]], [[die Kiwi]], [[die Feige]] (fig), [[der Granatapfel]] (pomegranate), [[die Avocado]], [[die Grapefruit]].
Regional words: in the north [[die Apfelsine]] for orange; in the south and Austria [[die Zwetschge]] for plum; in Austria [[die Marille]] for apricot.
notes.extra: About 25 fruit names, with the regional variants.

points: [[das Gemüse]] (vegetables) is a collective noun: singular, with das.
Basics: [[die Karotte]] or [[die Möhre]] (carrot), [[die Zwiebel]] (onion), [[die Kartoffel]], [[die Tomate]], [[die Gurke]] (cucumber), [[die Paprika]] (pepper), [[der Salat]] (lettuce).

More: [[die Bohne]] (bean), [[die Erbse]] (pea), [[der Mais]] (corn), [[der Kürbis]] (pumpkin), [[der Kohl]] (cabbage), [[der Blumenkohl]] (cauliflower), [[der Rosenkohl]] (Brussels sprouts), [[der Brokkoli]], [[der Spinat]], [[der Spargel]] (asparagus), [[die Zucchini]], [[die Aubergine]], [[der Knoblauch]] (garlic), [[der Ingwer]] (ginger), [[der Lauch]] (leek).
No plural: [[der Mais]], [[der Knoblauch]], [[der Spinat]], [[der Ingwer]].
Austria and southern Germany: [[der Erdapfel]] for potato; Austria also [[die Melanzani]] for aubergine.
notes.extra: About 30 vegetable names, with the Austrian and southern variants.

sections.text: Russian овощи and фрукты are plural. German [[das Gemüse]] and [[das Obst]] are singular, like one big heap: [[Das Gemüse ist billig.]] [[Das Obst ist gut.]]

sections.title: In Munich
sections.text: A bread roll is [[das Brötchen]] in most of Germany, but in Bavaria it's [[die Semmel]]. A pretzel is [[die Breze]]. At a Munich bakery: [[Zwei Semmeln und eine Breze, bitte.]]

sections.title: Meals
sections.text:
[[das Frühstück]] (breakfast), [[das Mittagessen]] (lunch), [[das Abendessen]] (dinner). [[das Essen]] is food in general, or a meal: [[Das Essen ist gut.]]

[[Zum Frühstück esse ich ein Brötchen.]] = For breakfast I have a roll. [[zum]] is a chunk here; Unit 6 explains it.

For amounts you can't count, there's no article: [[Ich esse Brot.]] [[Ich esse kein Fleisch.]] = I don't eat meat.

sections.title: Verbs that change their vowel
sections.text:
You know some already: [[sprechen]], [[du sprichst]] (Unit 1); [[es fängt an]], [[er sieht fern]] (Unit 3); and from the Unit 3 word cards, [[er schläft]], [[er trifft]].

The change happens **only** with [[du]] and [[er]]/[[sie]]/[[es]]. [[ich]], [[wir]], [[ihr]] and [[sie]]/[[Sie]] stay regular. There are three patterns:
- e becomes i: [[essen]], [[du isst]]; [[nehmen]], [[du nimmst]]; [[sprechen]], [[du sprichst]]
- e becomes ie: [[lesen]], [[du liest]]; [[sehen]], [[du siehst]]
- a becomes ä: [[fahren]], [[du fährst]]; [[schlafen]], [[du schläfst]]

The word list shows the change on the card: 'to eat (du isst, er isst)'.

[[nehmen]] changes more than the vowel: [[du nimmst]], [[er nimmt]], with mm and no h. And with [[essen]], [[du isst]] and [[er isst]] are the same.

[[fahren]] is to go by car, bus, train or bike: [[Ich fahre nach Hause.]] On foot it's [[gehen]]: [[Ich gehe nach Hause.]]

items.de: Zum Frühstück esse ich ein Brötchen mit Butter.
items.en: For breakfast I have a roll with butter.

items.de: Isst du Fleisch? - Nein, ich esse kein Fleisch.
items.en: Do you eat meat? - No, I don't eat meat.

items.de: Was nimmst du? - Ich nehme den Fisch.
items.en: What are you having? - I'll have the fish.

items.de: Am Abend liest er ein Buch.
items.en: In the evening he reads a book.

items.de: Am Samstag fährt sie nach Hause.
ich esse, du isst, er isst
items.en: I eat, you eat, he eats

items.de: ich nehme, du nimmst, er nimmt
items.en: I take, you take, he takes

items.de: ich lese, du liest, sie liest
items.en: I read, you read, she reads

items.de: ich fahre, du fährst, er fährt
items.en: I go, you go, he goes (by car, bus, train)

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: What do you eat for breakfast?
items.explanation: essen changes e to i: du isst.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap with nehmen: He's having the fish.
items.explanation: nehmen: er nimmt, with mm and no h.

items.question: Which sentence means 'She's reading a book'?
items.explanation: lesen changes e to ie: sie liest. (Sie lesen would be the polite you, or they.)

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: Are you going home on Saturday? (by train)
items.explanation: fahren changes a to ä: du fährst. By train, bus or car it's fahren.

items.question: Which article goes with Gemüse?
items.explanation: das Gemüse, and it's singular: Das Gemüse ist billig.
